title: 6'-O-caffeoylarbutin attenuates D-galactose-induced brain and liver damage in aging mice via regulating SIRT1/NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Wang, Yongpeng; Wang, Yongchao; Zhao, Tianrui; Zhou, Wenbing; Khan, Afsar; Cao, Jianxin; Liu, Yaping; Wang, Zhengxuan; Cheng, Guiguang
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物CA通过SIRT1/NF-kB通路缓解衰老小鼠肝脑损伤，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aging-related liver and brain damage caused by oxidative stress and inflammation significantly impacts health and quality of life. Natural bioactive compounds, such as 6'-O-caffeoylarbutin (CA), which is primarily distributed in Vaccinium species, have been studied for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study aims to investigate the protective effect on liver and brain damage induced by D-galactose (D-gal) in mice and to explore its potential molecular mechanisms. PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the protective effects of CA on D-galactose (D-gal)-induced liver and brain damage in mice and to explore its potential molecular mechanisms. METHODS: CA was prepared from Vaccinium dunalianum and identified using UHPLC-ESI-HR-MS/MS. Molecular docking and network pharmacology analysis were performed to predict the binding of CA with SIRT1 and NF-kappaB1 targets. In vivo, a D-gal-induced aging mouse model was established to evaluate the biochemical, oxidative stress, and inflammatory parameters. The effects of CA on oxidative stress and inflammation were examined through enzymatic activity assays, cytokine level measurements, and histopathological analysis. Western blotting was used to validate the involvement of the SIRT1/NF-kappaB pathway. RESULTS: CA treatment significantly alleviated liver and brain damage in D-gal-induced mice by decreasing AChE, AST, and ALT activities, improving organ indices, and reducing histopathological alterations. CA enhanced antioxidant defense by increasing SOD, CAT, and T-AOC activities, elevating GSH levels, and decreasing MDA content. Furthermore, CA suppressed the inflammatory response by downregulating IL-6 and TNF-alpha levels. Mechanistically, CA inhibited NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation and suppressed iNOS and COX-2 expression, likely via activation of the SIRT1 protein. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that CA protects against D-gal-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in liver and brain tissues via the SIRT1/NF-kappaB pathway, supporting its potential as a bioactive compound for preventing aging-related liver and brain damage.
abstract_zh: 背景：由氧化应激和炎症引起的衰老相关肝脑损伤显著影响健康和生活质量。天然生物活性化合物，如主要分布于越橘属（Vaccinium）物种中的6'-O-咖啡酰熊果苷（6'-O-caffeoylarbutin, CA），已被研究其抗氧化和抗炎特性。本研究旨在探讨其对D-半乳糖（D-galactose, D-gal）诱导的小鼠肝脑损伤的保护作用，并探索其潜在分子机制。目的：本研究旨在探讨CA对D-半乳糖（D-gal）诱导的小鼠肝脑损伤的保护作用，并探索其潜在分子机制。方法：从越橘（Vaccinium dunalianum）中制备CA，并使用UHPLC-ESI-HR-MS/MS进行鉴定。采用分子对接和网络药理学分析预测CA与SIRT1和NF-kappaB1靶点的结合。在体内，建立D-gal诱导的衰老小鼠模型，以评估生化、氧化应激和炎症参数。通过酶活性测定、细胞因子水平测量和组织病理学分析，检查CA对氧化应激和炎症的影响。使用Western blotting验证SIRT1/NF-kappaB通路的参与。结果：CA处理通过降低AChE、AST和ALT活性、改善器官指数和减少组织病理学改变，显著缓解D-gal诱导小鼠的肝脑损伤。CA通过增加SOD、CAT和T-AOC活性、提高GSH水平和降低MDA含量，增强抗氧化防御。此外，CA通过下调IL-6和TNF-alpha水平抑制炎症反应。机制上，CA抑制NF-kappaB p65磷酸化并抑制iNOS和COX-2表达，可能通过激活SIRT1蛋白实现。结论：本研究证明CA通过SIRT1/NF-kappaB通路保护肝脑组织免受D-gal诱导的氧化应激和炎症，支持其作为预防衰老相关肝脑损伤的生物活性化合物的潜力。
